instructions.name: initialize
docs: Create a basket's oracle. Upgrade authority only, once per basket.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Must be this program's upgrade authority.

accounts.name: program
docs: upgrade authority. Address-checked.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: `require_deployer`; absent under loader v4.

accounts.name: basket
docs: the index token's mint, which `adapter::validate_pool` requires the
pool to pair; for the mock it is only a label.

instructions.name: refresh_price
docs: Read the AMM and republish the price. PERMISSIONLESS: anyone may call
it, which is exactly why there is no privileged oracle key here — and
exactly why nothing in it may get cheaper by calling it more often.
Order of defences (each blocks a different attack):
1. one update per slot -> a second call in the same slot is a no-op
2. time-weighted TWAP -> a pushed spot counts only for the seconds it stays
3. clamp scaled by elapsed time -> the price cannot outrun the clock
4. minimum depth over the window -> liquidity must stay to count
5. divergence against the external median -> blocks sustained manipulation

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless by design: any keeper will do, and if ours goes down
someone else keeps the price alive.

accounts.name: amm_pool
docs: Adapters that keep reserves outside the pool account read them from
the remaining accounts (Raydium: vault 0, vault 1) and verify each.

instructions.name: set_external_median
docs: Publish the median of external fills, which is only the sanity bound.
If this feed fails, the market loses ONE defence and keeps working off
the AMM price. It never becomes a price source.

instructions.name: set_params
docs: Change the oracle's risk parameters. Admin only.

errors.name: EmptyPool
errors.msg: AMM pool is empty or has no fraction reserve

errors.name: PriceOverflow
errors.msg: Price does not fit in u64

errors.name: WrongAmmPool
errors.msg: AMM pool account differs from the one registered on the oracle

errors.name: AdapterBadAccount
errors.msg: AMM pool account has an unexpected layout

errors.name: AdapterWrongVault
errors.msg: Pool vault is missing or is not the vault the pool records

errors.name: AdapterWrongMint
errors.msg: Pool does not pair the oracle's basket mint, or a vault holds the wrong mint

errors.name: AdapterWrongAuthority
errors.msg: Pool vault is not owned by the AMM's own authority

errors.name: AdapterUnsupportedToken
errors.msg: Pool token uses a token program or decimals the oracle does not price

errors.name: AdapterPoolDisabled
errors.msg: Pool has swaps disabled, so its reserves are not a market price

errors.name: AdapterInsufficientVault
errors.msg: Pool vault holds less than the fees it owes

types.name: AmmAdapter
docs: Which external AMM the oracle reads. `Mock` exists because, as of day 1,
the on-chain layout of the real fraction pool is not confirmed — see
`docs/oracle.md`, "Blocker #1".

types.name: Observation
docs: A checkpoint of the running price integral.
The TWAP is `(cumulative_now - cumulative_then) / (now - then)`: every
spot price counts for exactly as long as it was in force. Averaging the
raw readings instead let one caller stuff the buffer with copies of a
pushed price. Checkpoints are spaced at least `window / 31` apart, so the
buffer always reaches back a full window however often anyone refreshes.

fields.name: ts
docs: Unix timestamp of the checkpoint.

fields.name: cumulative
docs: Sum of `spot * seconds` up to `ts`.

fields.name: depth
docs: Lowest AMM USDC reserve seen from `ts` until the next checkpoint. The
published depth is the minimum over the window, so liquidity added for
one transaction cannot buy open interest.

types.name: OracleAccount
docs: The oracle account. WRITTEN only by the `oracle` program.
`perp` and `clp-pool` read it through [`read_oracle`], never deserializing
by hand and never assuming how the price was computed.

fields.name: basket
docs: The basket this oracle prices.

fields.name: amm_pool
docs: External AMM pool account the reserves are read from.

fields.name: adapter
docs: Which adapter knows how to read `amm_pool`.

fields.name: admin
docs: Authority allowed to change parameters. Cannot write a price.

fields.name: price
docs: THE OFFICIAL PRICE, in WAD. Already through TWAP and clamp. This is
what liquidation and PnL use. Never the spot.

fields.name: twap
docs: Raw window TWAP, before the clamp. Diagnostics only.

fields.name: spot
docs: Last spot read from the AMM, unsmoothed. It enters the TWAP only for
the time it stays in force, starting at the NEXT refresh: a price
pushed for one transaction counts for the seconds until somebody
refreshes again, which is almost nothing.

fields.name: cumulative
docs: Running integral of `spot * seconds`. See [`Observation`].

fields.name: slow_twap
docs: A deliberately sluggish EMA of the price, used ONLY to mark the pool's
card sleeve. See [`OracleView::mark_price`] for why it exists.

fields.name: depth_usdc
docs: AMM USDC reserve, as the MINIMUM over the TWAP window. This is the
`R` in the depth ceiling. Liquidity counts once it has stayed.

fields.name: external_median
docs: Median of external fills. SECONDARY DEFENCE: a sanity bound only, never
a price source.

types.name: OracleParams
docs: Oracle configuration. WAD scale unless stated otherwise.

fields.name: twap_window_secs
docs: TWAP window in seconds. Spec: 1800 (30 min).

fields.name: max_tick_move
docs: Largest move accepted per `clamp_period_secs` of elapsed time. WAD.
Spec: 0.05.
Scaled by TIME, not by update. An earlier version allowed this much
per call, and `refresh_price` is permissionless: twelve calls in one
transaction moved the price 79.6%.

fields.name: max_staleness_secs
docs: Age at which the oracle goes `Stale`, in seconds. Spec: 900.

fields.name: min_pool_depth
docs: Minimum AMM depth, in native USDC. Spec: 25_000_000_000 ($25k).

fields.name: max_divergence
docs: Largest divergence tolerated against the external median. WAD. Spec: 0.15.

fields.name: slow_alpha
docs: EMA coefficient for [`OracleAccount::slow_twap`]. WAD.
Small on purpose. At 0.01 and a 30s refresh the slow price takes about
fifty minutes to follow a step change, which is the point: see
[`OracleView::mark_price`].
Applied per `clamp_period_secs` of elapsed time, never per call, so
refreshing more often does not drag it faster.

fields.name: clamp_period_secs
docs: The period `max_tick_move` and `slow_alpha` are expressed over, in
seconds. Spec: 15.

types.name: OracleState
docs: Why the oracle is or is not healthy. `Ok` is the only state that allows a
position to be opened.
